function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I don’t personally know anyone named Daniel—my knowledge is based on publicly available information up to my last update. If you have a specific Daniel in mind (for example, a public figure, a historical person, or someone in a particular field), let me know and I’ll do my best to share relevant facts or context!
message.reasoning: User asks: "do you know Daniel?" We need to respond appropriately. According to policy, we should not claim personal knowledge or familiarity with private individuals. We can say we don't personally know them. But we might ask clarifying question: "Which Daniel?" Or we can provide general info about common names. But we should not claim personal knowledge. So answer: I don't personally know anyone named Daniel; if you give more context, I can help.
